OyfBQmvr2Hc.summary: William Byrd presents at Papers We Love NYC on what he calls the most beautiful program ever written, a Lisp interpreter written in Lisp. He walks through the metacircular interpreter and related ideas, and demos relational programming and program synthesis near the end.
OyfBQmvr2Hc.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as an amazing talk that derives the essence of Lisp and shows miniKanren-style program synthesis.

ORzNZUeUHAM.summary: Not Just Bikes introduces the "stroad", a street-road hybrid common in the US and Canada that fails at both jobs. He contrasts it with Dutch design, where each road has a single purpose, and covers cost, danger and ugliness.
ORzNZUeUHAM.why: HN links it constantly as the standard introduction to stroads and Strong Towns-style arguments about car-centric design.

O5BJVO3PDeQ.summary: Internet Historian tells the story of No Man's Sky, from its over-hyped and badly received launch to years of updates by Hello Games that redeemed the game. It is a long, comedic mini-documentary.
O5BJVO3PDeQ.why: Frequently recommended as an entertaining account of a failed launch and recovery, especially in threads about Star Citizen and over-promising.

OSGv2VnC0go.summary: Raymond Hettinger's PyCon 2013 talk on transforming code into idiomatic Python through a series of before-and-after refactorings. It shows how to use iterators, dictionaries, named tuples and other language features well.
OSGv2VnC0go.why: HN treats it as a must-watch classic for writing Pythonic code, though somewhat dated for modern Python.

OkmNXy7er84.summary: 3Blue1Brown walks through a very hard Putnam competition problem and its elegant solution, emphasizing the visual intuition and the thought process behind solving it.
OkmNXy7er84.why: HN fans list it among their favorite 3Blue1Brown videos for showing how mathematical problem solving actually unfolds.

OoJsPvmFixU.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day gives a talk to an aerospace audience, comparing how Apollo was engineered and managed with NASA's Artemis program. He raises concerns about unresolved details, the number of launches and in-orbit fuel transfer needed to reach the Moon, and the loss of institutional knowledge.
OoJsPvmFixU.why: Commenters point to it whenever Artemis, SLS or Starship refueling comes up, as a candid and critical engineering assessment delivered directly to NASA.

ON0A1dsQOV0.summary: Dirk Hohndel explains why the Subsurface dive log project migrated from Gtk to Qt, the obstacles encountered, and advice for other applications frustrated with Gtk. It is a linux.conf.au 2014 talk.
ON0A1dsQOV0.why: Go-to reference in GTK versus Qt debates, valued for a candid account from experienced developers who tried both toolkits.

O133ppiVnWY.summary: Physicist Al Bartlett's well-known lecture on the arithmetic of exponential growth, applied to population, energy consumption and resource depletion. He argues that steady percentage growth cannot be sustained on a finite planet and that most public discussion ignores this.
O133ppiVnWY.why: HN commenters cite it as a mind-changing introduction to exponential growth, though some note his peak oil predictions did not pan out.

OjMPJVmXxV8.summary: A long video essay by Natalie Wynn of ContraPoints on cancel culture, drawing on her own experience of being pile-on targeted by other leftists. It is theatrical and discursive, mixing argument with performance.
OjMPJVmXxV8.why: HN commenters recommend it as a more thoughtful, balanced and personal take on cancel culture than usual discussion.

ORp3q1Oaezw.summary: Black musician Daryl Davis tells how a chance encounter led him to befriend Ku Klux Klan members and seek the source of racial hate. He argues that sitting down and talking with people can change them.
ORp3q1Oaezw.why: Recommended in moderation and deplatforming debates as a case for engagement and compassion over exclusion.

OUNXFHpUhu8.summary: Climate Town traces the history of American parking minimums, how they came from shaky research and ITE guides, and how they shape zoning, cities and housing costs. It is a long, comedic video essay.
OUNXFHpUhu8.why: Recommended as a fun but well-researched explanation of why parking requirements are arbitrary and harmful.

OmJ-4B-mS-Y.summary: An animated 11-minute tour of the whole field of mathematics as a single map, showing how pure and applied math and their sub-fields relate to each other.
OmJ-4B-mS-Y.why: Recommended to people asking how to self-learn math as a quick bird's-eye overview of the field.

OKY6BGcx37k.summary: An HBO special in which Jerry Seinfeld, Chris Rock, Ricky Gervais and Louis CK discuss the craft of stand-up comedy. They talk about writing jokes, technique and how they handle old material.
OKY6BGcx37k.why: HN points to it as a rare look at how top comedians think about craft, motivation and process.

ObhK8lUfIlc.summary: A GDC 2018 talk by Valve's John McDonald on VACNet, a deep learning system that analyzes CS:GO gameplay to detect cheaters. It covers how the model is trained on human-reviewed Overwatch cases and how its output feeds human moderation.
ObhK8lUfIlc.why: HN points to it as the definitive example of server-side, behavioral, non-invasive anti-cheat using machine learning, often as a counterpoint to kernel-level anti-cheat.

Obt-vMVdM8s.summary: David Beazley's PyCon 2010 talk explains how the Python Global Interpreter Lock works and shows experiments where multithreaded code runs slower, even on more cores, due to lock contention and context-switching overhead.
Obt-vMVdM8s.why: The canonical recommendation for understanding the GIL, praised both for its clarity and for how well it explains a deep technical topic.

O-2tpwW0kmU.summary: Slaughterbots is a short sci-fi film in which swarms of cheap autonomous drones are programmed to kill targets by profile. It was made as arms-control advocacy against autonomous weapons.
O-2tpwW0kmU.why: HN keeps citing it whenever drone swarms, autonomous weapons or AI warfare come up, as a believable depiction of where this leads.

OMPfEXIlTVE.summary: Sandi Metz argues that hidden assumptions in code are missing concepts, and shows how to name and expose them so code is easier to understand and change. It covers null objects and messages in Ruby.
OMPfEXIlTVE.why: HN recommends it as a funny, smart and well-constructed talk on abstraction, duplication and object-oriented design.

OQ5jsbhAv_M.summary: Erik Demaine's MIT 6.006 lecture introducing dynamic programming through Fibonacci numbers and shortest paths. It covers memoization, subproblems and optimal substructure.
OQ5jsbhAv_M.why: Recommended as a clear introduction to dynamic programming from a well-regarded instructor.

Oo0jm1PPRuo.summary: Veritasium explains why the kilogram is being redefined in terms of Planck's constant rather than a physical metal artifact. It visits NIST to show the Kibble balance and why measuring mass precisely is hard.
Oo0jm1PPRuo.why: Praised as an excellent, accessible account of why the kilogram's definition changed, in redefinition threads.

OqjcrfKjobY.summary: A short overview of Tabs Outliner, a Chrome extension that shows browser tabs and windows as a nestable tree. It demonstrates organizing, saving and restoring tabs.
OqjcrfKjobY.why: Commenters who struggle with tab overload use it to show what tree-based tab management looks like and recommend the extension.

O61WihMRdjM.summary: Weber State's Professor Kelly explains the Toyota RAV4 Hybrid transaxle, including its planetary gearset eCVT and all nine operating modes. It also covers how the engine reaches nearly 40 percent thermal efficiency.
O61WihMRdjM.why: HN points to it as the clearest hands-on explanation of how Toyota hybrids work.

OP4CKn86qGY.summary: Adam Savage answers viewer questions on dealing with condescending colleagues, focusing on dismissive phrases such as 'why don't you just' and 'I would have'. He explains why such language undermines the person receiving it.
OP4CKn86qGY.why: HN recommends it whenever 'why don't you just...' comes up as an example of arrogant, dismissive advice.

OQQ-W_63UgQ.summary: The first lecture of Stanford's Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning course, taught by Chris Manning and Richard Socher. It introduces NLP and word vectors, including SVD, skip-gram, CBOW, negative sampling and word2vec.
OQQ-W_63UgQ.why: Recommended as one of the best free courses for learning modern deep learning for NLP.

OWXoRSIxyIU.summary: Veritasium debunks common climate change myths in under seven minutes, with references to NASA and published research. Topics include CO2 sources, sea ice and 1970s predictions of cooling.
OWXoRSIxyIU.why: Used as a short, well-made rebuttal to common global warming arguments in climate threads.

O_azyt1JhI0.summary: Video of the March 2014 Senate Defense Subcommittee hearing on National Security Space Launch programs. Elon Musk of SpaceX testifies alongside ULA's CEO, a GAO official and a policy expert, on launch contracts and Russian engines.
O_azyt1JhI0.why: HN points to it as an entertaining and informative look at the SpaceX versus ULA rivalry.

ObvxPSQNMGc.summary: A Capella Science parody of Camila Cabello's Havana, retold as a song about molecular machines and nanotechnology. It features animations of rotaxanes, catenanes and molecular switches, and comes with footnotes.
ObvxPSQNMGc.why: HN commenters recommend it as a catchy, accurate piece of science edutainment, and admire its footnote practice.

OqEeIG8aPPk.summary: A 1994 talk by systems thinker Russ Ackoff, who knew W. Edwards Deming, on continuous versus discontinuous improvement. It ends with an unexpected lesson.
OqEeIG8aPPk.why: HN favors it as a compact, quotable management and systems-thinking talk, often cited for doing the right thing versus doing the wrong thing right.

OxhTQdcieQE.summary: Brian Cardarella's RailsConf 2016 talk on why and how teams can move from Rails to Elixir and Phoenix. It covers performance gains without losing productivity and how to introduce Phoenix in an organization.
OxhTQdcieQE.why: HN points Rails developers to it as a real-world case for migrating to Phoenix, backed by numbers.

O45LaFsaqMA.summary: Vladimir Voevodsky's IAS lecture starts from Godel's second incompleteness theorem to explore whether first-order arithmetic could be inconsistent. It motivates his vision of univalent foundations and computer-checked proofs.
O45LaFsaqMA.why: Recommended as a thought-provoking lecture from a Fields medalist on the foundations of mathematics and formal proof verification.

OBPpRqxY8Uw.summary: Stanford physicist Leonard Susskind gives the first of two mini-lectures on "ER = EPR", the idea that quantum entanglement and wormholes are related. It covers what lies behind black hole horizons.
OBPpRqxY8Uw.why: HN people point to it as the more detailed follow-up when articles touch on entanglement, holography and black holes.

OFgxAFdxYAQ.summary: Cliff Click walks through a small performance example on a modern out-of-order CPU. He covers pipelining, ILP, CISC vs RISC, multicore, and why cache misses and the memory subsystem dominate performance.
OFgxAFdxYAQ.why: Recommended as an accessible refresher on how modern hardware and caches affect software performance.

OHPkdMGI6D4.summary: Corridor Crew VFX artists react to the visual effects of the 2021 Dune and compare them with David Lynch's 1984 version. They discuss which effects were practical and which were CGI.
OHPkdMGI6D4.why: HN commenters cite it in debates about practical effects versus CGI, as a fun comparison of old and new Dune.

OINAk2xl8Bc.summary: Yuta explains what Japan's 99% conviction rate actually means, noting that prosecutors drop cases unless confidence is very high. He argues that the number is widely misunderstood and cites his sources.
OINAk2xl8Bc.why: Recommended as a sourced, nuanced corrective whenever the Japanese justice system's conviction rate is raised.

OLLwG_SN8oo.summary: Sam Aaron, creator of Sonic Pi, gives a demo-heavy GOTO Chicago 2018 talk on live coding music. He covers the history of Sonic Pi, how it evolved, and what it can do for education and professional musicians.
OLLwG_SN8oo.why: HN recommends it as the best talk from Sonic Pi's creator, with live-coding examples and technical and teaching insights.

OsFEV35tWsg.summary: Psychologist Philip Zimbardo explains how ordinary people can be pushed into doing evil by situations and systems. He draws on the Stanford prison experiment and unseen Abu Ghraib photos, then turns to the opposite case: how ordinary people can become heroes.
OsFEV35tWsg.why: HN uses it to argue that systems rather than bad apples drive cruelty, and for its section on how anonymity changes behavior.

OyFJWRnt_AY.summary: A university lecture from CS480/680 by Pascal Poupart on attention mechanisms and transformer networks, worked through on a chalkboard.
OyFJWRnt_AY.why: HN recommends it to newcomers as a clear explanation of attention, including the query/key/value intuition.

ODSJsviD_SU.summary: Tesla's full AI Day 2022 presentation, covering the Tesla Bot hardware and software, Full Self-Driving planning and perception, the occupancy network, data labeling, simulation and Dojo training infrastructure.
ODSJsviD_SU.why: HN uses it as primary-source evidence on how Tesla's vision-based driving stack and training pipeline work.

OL6-x0modwY.summary: A one-minute clip of Richard Feynman describing the scientific method: guess a law, compute its consequences, and compare with experiment. If it disagrees with experiment, it is wrong.
OL6-x0modwY.why: HN quotes it as the crispest statement of what science is, usually when a theory clashes with evidence.

Ocq3NeudsVk.summary: Tantacrul examines sonification, the practice of turning data into sound or music, and critiques how scientists and musicians, including NASA and CERN projects, use it well and poorly.
Ocq3NeudsVk.why: Recommended as an incisive look at the real potential and common misuse of data sonification, often brought up in threads on space sonifications.

Og6cTlwBTrk.summary: A short film following Moroccan artisans from Fez as they build a traditional 15th-century-style Moroccan court inside the Metropolitan Museum of Art. It shows zellij tilework and other traditional techniques.
Og6cTlwBTrk.why: Shared as a satisfying look at craftsmen taking pride in traditional handmade tile mosaics.

Oie1ZXWceqM.summary: A SIGGRAPH Asia 2013 research demo of 3-Sweep, a tool for extracting editable 3D objects from a single photo using a few user strokes. It predates modern AI image tools.
Oie1ZXWceqM.why: HN recalls it as a mind-blowing pre-AI demo of 2D-to-3D object extraction.

OtLvtMqWNz8.summary: A film-analysis video essay linking Blade Runner 2049's Cells Interlinked sequence to Nabokov's Pale Fire. It examines the poetry and meaning behind the film's references.
OtLvtMqWNz8.why: HN recommends it as the best video essay on the film's use of Pale Fire.

Ox5P7QyL774.summary: A 1995 Sun Microsystems film about the Self programming language, a prototype-based Smalltalk relative, showing its live, graphical programming environment.
Ox5P7QyL774.why: HN uses it as the canonical demo of Self's integrated, direct-manipulation environment whenever prototypal inheritance or live programming comes up.

O1lZ9n2bxWA.summary: Technology Connections explains why North American tail light rules, which allow red turn signals and flashing brake lights, make signals ambiguous. He argues for amber signals and cites studies showing a safety benefit.
O1lZ9n2bxWA.why: HN points to it as the informative explanation of US turn signal quirks whenever signal design comes up.

O4Ko7NW2yQo.summary: A PBS Space Time episode explaining the Fermilab Muon g-2 results and why a discrepancy with the Standard Model prediction could point to new physics.
O4Ko7NW2yQo.why: Recommended as an accessible but not oversimplified explanation of the muon g-2 experiment, by a channel aimed at curious physics enthusiasts.

OB-bdWKwXsU.summary: Bjarne Stroustrup's keynote at Going Native 2012 covers the ideas behind C++11, including using types to prevent errors and simplifying code with the STL.
OB-bdWKwXsU.why: Cited as a good talk on the thinking behind C++11 and on using the type system to prevent bugs; some other mentions quote it critically.

OINa46HeWg8.summary: A two-minute satirical short film in which a woman leaves her phone at home and notices how everyone around her is absorbed in their screens. It became a viral comment on phone distraction and social disconnection.
OINa46HeWg8.why: Cited in threads about phone addiction and distraction as a classic, widely seen illustration of the problem.

OJv8rFap0Nw.summary: A Lambda Days keynote by Simon Peyton Jones and Tim Sweeney introducing Verse, Epic's functional logic language for the metaverse. It covers existential variables, unification and expressions yielding multiple values.
OJv8rFap0Nw.why: HN recommends it as an interesting look at functional logic programming with wide implications for game programming.

OMcjxe8slYI.summary: An RTE documentary on Chuck Feeney, the Atlantic Philanthropies founder who secretly gave away his fortune. It covers his Giving While Living approach and his gifts to Irish education.
OMcjxe8slYI.why: Recommended in threads on Feeney as a decent, thorough account of his anonymous giving.

OMi6xgdSbMA.summary: Lucas Pope, creator of Return of the Obra Dinn, explains in Ars Technica's War Stories how localizing the game's logbook nearly sank the project.
OMi6xgdSbMA.why: Recommended for its insight into game design and cited as a vivid example of how tricky localization can be.

OOK5xkFijPc.summary: Technology Connections explains the difference between power (watts) and energy (watt-hours) and why confusing them leads to errors. It runs about 52 minutes and uses everyday examples.
OOK5xkFijPc.why: HN points to it whenever a thread mixes up power and energy, such as battery specs and solar generation.

OOeBJ8mDr8Q.summary: Builder Matt Risinger freezes water-filled copper and PEX piping capped with SharkBite fittings to see which survives. The video compares how each pipe type handles freezing.
OOeBJ8mDr8Q.why: Recommended as an interesting experiment showing PEX tolerates freezing better than copper.

OTVE5iPMKLg.summary: CGP Grey's short explainer arguing that caffeine addiction is mostly harmless and may even be beneficial. It covers what caffeine does in the body.
OTVE5iPMKLg.why: HN links it in caffeine threads as a quick, clear explanation of caffeine's effects.

OWJCfOvochA.summary: IBM's Dr. Talia Gershon explains quantum computing to five people of increasing expertise: a child, teen, college student, grad student and professional. The WIRED series format moves from simple analogies to technical detail.
OWJCfOvochA.why: HN points to it both as an approachable quantum computing intro and as an example of explaining one concept at multiple levels.

ObiqJzfyACM.summary: Vsauce explores math through card tricks and big numbers, including an animation of how enormous 52 factorial, the number of deck orderings, really is.
ObiqJzfyACM.why: Cited for its well-known attempt to convey the size of 52 factorial.

OgRFOjVzvm0.summary: A short Portuguese-language excerpt of Gerald Sussman's 2016 NYC Lisp Meetup talk explaining why MIT replaced the Scheme-based 6.001 (SICP) course with Python courses. The full talk is linked in the description.
OgRFOjVzvm0.why: HN uses it as the canonical explanation from Sussman himself of why SICP ended at MIT.

OkEdyq3UE5M.summary: Mike and Jay of RedLetterMedia discuss Starship Troopers, covering its legacy, why people like or dislike it, and its reading as sci-fi action satire versus the Heinlein book.
OkEdyq3UE5M.why: Pointed to as a good analysis of the film's satire and layers when Starship Troopers or Heinlein come up.

OqmdLcyES_Q.summary: An animated adaptation of Captain David Marquet's talk on greatness, based on his book Turn the Ship Around!. It argues for pushing decision-making down to the people doing the work instead of controlling everything from the top.
OqmdLcyES_Q.why: HN commenters cite it as a compact illustration of empowered, decentralized leadership, for founders and for managers who try to control everything.

OsDy-4L6-tQ.summary: Onslaught's Bad Apple 64 is a Commodore 64 demo that streams over 2000 frames of the Bad Apple animation from a single disk side at 12fps, with each frame packed to around 70 bytes.
OsDy-4L6-tQ.why: Shared as an impressive example of squeezing video and compression onto a 1 MHz 8-bit machine in Bad Apple porting threads.

Ot4qdCs54ZE.summary: An Economics Explained video arguing that the Netherlands shows taxes alone can't reduce wealth inequality. It distinguishes income inequality from wealth inequality and discusses the Gini index.
Ot4qdCs54ZE.why: HN uses it to explain the difference between income and wealth inequality, though some pair it with a rebuttal.

OyBNmecVtdU.summary: A high-quality recording of President Eisenhower's January 1961 farewell address, including his warning about the unwarranted influence of the military-industrial complex. The uploader marks the key passage at 8:41.
OyBNmecVtdU.why: HN commenters link it as the primary source for the phrase 'military-industrial complex' and urge people to hear the full speech rather than the soundbite.

OO18F4aKGzQ.summary: The official video for Brother Ali's 'Uncle Sam Goddamn', a politically charged rap song critiquing the United States, produced by Ant.
OO18F4aKGzQ.why: Shared in surveillance and civil-liberties threads as a powerful rap critique of the US.

OP0U62oiBlM.summary: DW Documentary on the roughly 6,300 ships sunk in World War II that are now rusting and leaking oil into the seas. Scientists investigate contamination and the risk of a huge oil spill.
OP0U62oiBlM.why: Recommended as a fascinating watch in threads on leaking wrecks and oil spills.

OaGp5_Sfbss.summary: The official trailer for The True Cost, a documentary on the fast fashion industry and who pays for cheap clothing. It touches on garment worker conditions and the Rana Plaza collapse.
OaGp5_Sfbss.why: HN cites the film as a source on fast fashion exploitation and pollution.

OpEB6hCpIGM.summary: Real Engineering explains why biofuels, especially corn ethanol, are a poor energy source, looking at energy inputs, efficiency and carbon cost.
OpEB6hCpIGM.why: Linked in fuel and aviation threads as the full story on why ethanol and biofuels are energy-negative or inefficient.

OxGsU8oIWjY.summary: Veritasium shows how Hilbert's infinite hotel can still run out of room, using infinite buses of guests. It explains the surprising answer in a short animated segment.
OxGsU8oIWjY.why: HN mentions it as a related, well-made Veritasium video when infinity and Hilbert's hotel come up.

O9upVbGSBFo.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Brian Kernighan, co-author of The C Programming Language and co-creator of AWK and AMPL. They discuss Unix, C, Go and his memoir on the history of Unix.
O9upVbGSBFo.why: Mentioned as a favorite podcast episode and as a source of firsthand computing history, such as timesharing.

OA8dNFiVaF0.summary: A 2001 University of Miami experiment ignites a leak from a gasoline fuel line in one car and a leak from a hydrogen connector in another. The hydrogen fire burns out quickly while the gasoline fire consumes its car.
OA8dNFiVaF0.why: HN cites it in hydrogen car debates, with some seeing it as evidence of relative safety and others finding it unconvincing.

OBfB2MJw3qg.summary: Kalman Reti, one of the last Symbolics developers, gives a roughly hour-long talk on Symbolics Lisp machines. It covers the machines and their environment from an insider's perspective.
OBfB2MJw3qg.why: HN recommends it to anyone curious about Lisp machines, since it comes from someone who worked at Symbolics.

OFvXuyITwBI.summary: Marques Brownlee shares his hands-on impressions of Apple's $3500 Vision Pro headset after trying it. He covers the spatial computing experience, eye tracking, and how it compares to other devices.
OFvXuyITwBI.why: HN used it as an early, credible hands-on report showing the headset roughly matched Apple's demos.

OHKKcd3sx2c.summary: Linus Tech Tips explains how Windows Modern Standby causes laptops to drain battery while asleep, arguing it makes Windows laptops hard to recommend compared to MacBooks.
OHKKcd3sx2c.why: HN links it as the standard reference whenever laptop sleep and battery drain on Windows come up, including the later point that nothing has improved.

OX31kZbAXsA.summary: Linus Tech Tips tests whether higher frame rates and refresh rates improve gaming performance, using Shroud and other players on aim and reaction tests at 60, 144 and 240Hz. The video is sponsored by Nvidia.
OX31kZbAXsA.why: HN commenters cite it as informal evidence that higher refresh rates measurably help both pro and casual players, even though it is more entertainment than rigorous science.

OXS8ljif9b8.summary: A roughly 14-minute interview with OpenBSD founder Theo de Raadt at ruBSD 2013. He talks about making painful changes, getting real feedback, mitigation techniques compared to other OSs, and virtualization.
OXS8ljif9b8.why: Pointed to in OpenBSD and virtualization threads for Theo's candid views on security mitigations and supporting modern x86 VMs.

OXzfvYoFQFo.summary: Josh Wardle, later the creator of Wordle, talks at SF Tech Poetics about why April Fools' Day in Silicon Valley is often lame. He shares lessons from building The Button and Place at Reddit.
OXzfvYoFQFo.why: HN points to it as a pre-Wordle look at Wardle's thinking on designing online spaces, and as a brief postmortem of r/place.

O_TjBNjc9Bo.summary: A 30-minute condensed version of the documentary I.O.U.S.A., which examines the growing US national debt and its consequences.
O_TjBNjc9Bo.why: Shared as a quick way to see the film's fiscal warnings, sometimes as an example of ignored warnings.

OhnjMdzGusc.summary: Jay Leno takes a host for a spin in his restored 1909 Baker Electric car on My Classic Car. It shows an early electric vehicle and what driving one is like.
OhnjMdzGusc.why: HN brings it up in electric vehicle threads as proof that electric cars date back over a century, with Leno an entertaining guide.

OjkzfeJz66o.summary: William Li presents anti-angiogenesis, the idea of cutting off the blood supply that feeds tumors, and argues that certain foods can help do this. It is a TED-Ed version of his TED talk.
OjkzfeJz66o.why: Mentioned as an interesting talk when threads touch on cancer, diet and fasting research.

Olj8arvfYj4.summary: A Half as Interesting explainer on the US program that drops millions of sterile screwworm flies over Panama every week to keep the parasite out of North America.
Olj8arvfYj4.why: Cited in screwworm threads as a short description of the sterile-insect barrier system that worked for decades.

OmZOZjHjT5E.summary: A short Cracked video arguing, tongue in cheek, that the world of the film Idiocracy would actually be a utopia. It plays with the movie's premise and today's politics.
OmZOZjHjT5E.why: Cited in passing to support the half-serious argument that Idiocracy's world is a utopia.

OrG7oG8Tvp8.summary: Matt Risinger covers installing a Zehnder ERV fresh-air system in a tight passive house, explaining balanced ventilation, the benefits of heat recovery and the costs involved.
OrG7oG8Tvp8.why: Pointed to in HVAC and indoor-air threads as a hands-on look at high-end ventilation and ERV installation.

Os7FE3J-U5Q.summary: Andy Keep's Clojure/Conj talk on writing a nanopass compiler, built from many single-task passes with formally defined intermediate languages. It covers the framework's origins in a compiler teaching course at Indiana University.
Os7FE3J-U5Q.why: Cited alongside compiler-construction resources as the go-to talk on the nanopass approach used in Chez Scheme.

O37yJBFRrfg.summary: A short CGP Grey explainer on the overlapping and inconsistent membership arrangements of European countries across the EU, Schengen, the euro and the EEA. It shows why "the EU" is full of exceptions.
O37yJBFRrfg.why: Cited as a fast, entertaining explanation of EU membership tiers when EU politics comes up.

ODZBL80JPqw.summary: Second half of a demonstration of the 1982 Xerox Star user interface. It shows how the Star differed from the later Lisa and Mac interfaces, with strengths in networking and printing and little direct manipulation.
ODZBL80JPqw.why: Listed among historical GUI and Smalltalk videos and cited for early features such as math in word processing and the Mesa-programmed Star.

ONZcjs1Pjmk.summary: The video accompanying the SIGGRAPH 2012 paper on Eulerian Video Magnification. It amplifies subtle changes in ordinary video, such as skin color shifts from a heartbeat, to reveal pulse and tiny motions.
ONZcjs1Pjmk.why: Cited as the canonical demonstration of pulling out invisible signals like pulse from video, with commenters imagining other applications.

OPcV9uIY5i4.summary: A tool-assisted speedrun of Super Mario World that achieves arbitrary code execution through frame-precise controller inputs, finishing in 2:25. It was also performed live on real hardware at AGDQ 2014.
OPcV9uIY5i4.why: Cited as the classic example of arbitrary code execution inside a game, with later runs injecting Pong, Snake and Flappy Bird.

OQUO1DSwYN0.summary: A WSJ interview in which Apple's Craig Federighi explains Apple's CSAM scanning and child-safety features, including neural hashes and safety vouchers, and defends them against backlash.
OQUO1DSwYN0.why: Mostly cited critically, as Apple's own defense of its scanning plans, which commenters found out of touch or unconvincing; one commenter says it adds nuance.

OR4jPtrDCLo.summary: A short clip of the audience at Valve's 2017 announcement of Artifact, a Dota 2 card game, reacting with visible disappointment. The footage captures the awkward silence and the logo reveal.
OR4jPtrDCLo.why: Cited as comedic evidence that Valve's own core fans were unenthused by Artifact, and later as an early warning sign of its failure.

OR5ZUl0Q-NI.summary: Louis Rossmann visits Apple Authorized Service Providers to see what repairs they can actually do. He finds, for example, that an iPhone 6 headphone jack is not repairable and requires an expensive board replacement.
OR5ZUl0Q-NI.why: Cited in right-to-repair discussions to show that authorized repair centers mostly swap units rather than repair them.

OS4O8rGRLf8.summary: A C-SPAN clip from a joint press conference with Olaf Scholz in which President Biden says that if Russia invades Ukraine, there will no longer be a Nord Stream 2. Pressed on how, he promises it can be done.
OS4O8rGRLf8.why: Repeatedly cited in Nord Stream sabotage threads as evidence of stated US intent toward the pipeline.

OW-atKrg0T4.summary: A 1997 Computer History Museum lecture in which Larry Tesler and Chris Espinosa recount how the Apple human interface was born, from the Lisa through the Macintosh. It covers design decisions such as discoverability and the standard editing keys.
OW-atKrg0T4.why: HN commenters cite it as a primary source on Lisa and Mac interface history, and a transcription of it was itself discussed on HN.

OWwOJlOI1nU.summary: A short clip of the robot's famous warning line 'Danger, Will Robinson!' from the 1960s TV series Lost in Space.
OWwOJlOI1nU.why: Used purely as a joke reference when someone should have heard an internal warning voice.

OXZYvrue1BE.summary: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian responds in a short interview to Anderson Cooper's on-air criticism of Reddit over child exploitation content.
OXZYvrue1BE.why: Not recommended; HN uses it as a critical example of Ohanian deflecting blame for Reddit's content problems.

OXtq4a8829g.summary: A friendlyjordies video on the legal fight between Jordan Shanks and then-Deputy Premier John Barilaro, including footage of the arrest of the creator by police. It is presented from one side.
OXtq4a8829g.why: Linked as footage of the arrest of an Australian online journalist, in threads about press freedom and state power.

OYecfV3ubP8.summary: The famous 1984 Apple Macintosh television commercial, framed as a rebellion against an Orwellian Big Brother. This copy was uploaded to YouTube just after the site launched.
OYecfV3ubP8.why: HN mostly uses it as a cultural reference, either as a favorite tech ad or as irony when criticizing Apple's later restrictiveness.

OeC1yAaWG34.summary: A comedy segment where Eddie Izzard travels to Friesland to try speaking Old English, claiming English originated in Holland and buying a cow to prove it.
OeC1yAaWG34.why: HN uses it as a joke reference in threads about the history of the English language.

Og847HVwRSI.summary: An animated ranking of the most popular programming languages from 1965 to 2019, built from popularity indexes, GitHub access data and historical surveys.
Og847HVwRSI.why: Cited as a data source for historical language popularity, though not as a recommendation.

OhESSZIXvCA.summary: Linus Tech Tips compares Microsoft's Surface Pro X (SQ2) with the Apple M1 MacBook Air, focusing on how Windows on Arm and x86 emulation perform against Apple's Arm hardware. The verdict is that the Surface falls well short.
OhESSZIXvCA.why: Cited as evidence of how poorly Windows x86 emulation on Arm performed in 2021 compared with Apple's M1 and Rosetta.

OoETMCosULQ.summary: A three-minute student film from Campus MovieFest showing drivers in every lane holding exactly the speed limit on an Atlanta-area interstate and the traffic jam that results.
OoETMCosULQ.why: Used as a demonstration of how everyone obeying the speed limit disrupts traffic flow.

OobLb1McxnI.summary: Charlie Miller and Chris Valasek present their DEF CON 23 talk on remotely compromising an unmodified Jeep, pivoting from the entertainment system to the vehicle's internal networks to send control messages. They aim to show the reality of car hacking.
OobLb1McxnI.why: HN uses it as the canonical reference that modern connected cars can be attacked remotely.

OopTOjnD3qY.summary: A Waymo clip, sped up 3x, showing its autonomous car stopping at a broken traffic light and proceeding on a police officer's hand signals.
OopTOjnD3qY.why: HN cites it as evidence that self-driving cars can obey traffic cops, though some call the scenario idealized.

OqtNleXhTRE.summary: Linus Tech Tips tests whether USB Type-C connectors are more durable than Micro-B by repeatedly plugging and unplugging them. In the test, Micro-B failed at around 8000 insertions while USB-C kept working.
OqtNleXhTRE.why: HN cites it whenever someone asks whether USB-C holds up better than micro USB, as a small sample but concrete test.

Ow0lr63y4Mw.summary: A classic Bob Newhart comedy sketch in which a therapist's only advice to a patient is to 'stop it'.
Ow0lr63y4Mw.why: Posted as a joke reply in threads where someone asks how to stop a habit or feeling.
